## Different ways to cite the text.

### Example: 1

several studies show increase the prductivity. [@s21113758]

### Example: 2

For multiple citation: [@s21113758; @s18082674]

### Example: 3

1.  parenthetical: ... results ([@s18082674]).
2.  Narrative: smith ([@s21113758]) found ...

## Cross-reference figure and tables

```{r}
#| label: fig:salinity
#| fig-cap: "germination rate vs salinity"
x <- c(12,23,43,43,24,14)
y <- c(1,2,3,4,2,5)
plot(x,y)
```

### References in the text

Figure \@ref(fig:salinity) shows that germination decreases with salinity.

## Adding footnote to the doucument. This can be two types.

### Inline footnotes

this is a inline footnote. [^1]

[^1]: this footnote will show there in the line

### Numaric footnotes

1.  this is footnote no one. [^2]
2.  this is footnote no two. [^3]

[^2]: somethings about the footnote 1

[^3]: somethings about the footnote 2
